## Story Goal

Deliver **Quick Replies** as reusable response templates that support Agents can browse, search, select, and **insert into a Ticket response composer** without ever auto-sending a message.

In scope:
1. Backend CRUD for Quick Reply templates (id, title/name, body text, active flag, timestamps).
2. Authorization via a new pair of permissions (View / Manage) that plug into the existing `HasPermission` policy provider.
3. Frontend list/manage screens under Agent Desk.
4. A **Quick Reply picker** on the Ticket detail page that inserts the selected template's text into the existing reply/composer field. The Agent can edit before submitting.
5. Empty state, search/filter, and audit hooks matching existing conventions.

Out of scope: automatic sending on any channel (Email, SMS, WhatsApp, Live Chat), AI suggestions, notifications, tasks/reminders, team collaboration.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty search** — service returns full list (ordered by title). Verified in `QuickRepliesService.ListAsync`.
- **Whitespace-only title / body** — server rejects via `[Required]` + `StringLength`; front-end form should also trim before submit.
- **Duplicate title (case-insensitive)** — service returns validation error; controller maps to `409` or `400` matching `TicketCategoriesService` behaviour. UI surfaces the message under the Title field.
- **Inactive quick reply** — hidden from the Ticket composer picker (`isActive=true` filter). Still visible in the management list when the "Show inactive" filter is on.
- **User without `quickreplies.view`** — cannot see the menu entry (AppLayout guard), cannot open the picker in `TicketDetailPage`, and API returns 403 via `HasPermission` attribute.
- **User with `view` but not `manage`** — list is read-only; New/Edit/Delete controls hidden; API returns 403 on write.
- **Very long body (near 5000 chars)** — insertion must not truncate. Textarea should remain scrollable.
- **Concurrent edit** — last-write-wins, matching `TicketCategoriesService`. No optimistic-concurrency token in this story.
- **Composer without caret ref** — inserter falls back to `value + '\n' + body` and re-sets state.
- **Empty catalogue** — list page shows empty state; ticket picker shows `"No quick replies available."` without an error.
- **Unicode / RTL** — the user's account uses Arabic locale (Marwa); ensure the textarea and the picker render RTL content correctly (relies on the existing CSS in `frontend/src/theme.ts` / `frontend/src/index.css`; no story-specific override).
- **Auto-send guard** — insertion path must never call any `send` / `submit` API. Enforced by not importing/using the ticket send action in `QuickReplyPicker.tsx`.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** apply the new `AddQuickReplies` migration (`dotnet ef database update -p src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure -s src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api`). Seeder grants permissions on next boot.
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef database update <PreviousMigrationName> -p src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure -s src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api` (previous being `20260831073526_AddTicketHistory`). Optionally revoke the two new permissions from role assignments (safe to leave; unused permissions have no effect once endpoints are gone).
- **Half-applied state:** if the DB migration ran but the API is rolled back, orphan table `QuickReplies` remains — harmless. If the API is deployed but migration was not applied, the API startup log will surface EF migration warnings; run the migration and restart.

## Correction (post-implementation) — Agent gets `quickreplies.manage`, not just `View`

The plan above (§7 Seed permissions, §5 Controller) modeled `QuickReplies.Manage` on `Tickets.CategoriesManage`'s admin-only master-data convention — Agent was granted `View` only, so an Agent could browse and insert quick replies via the picker but not create/edit/delete them.

Feedback after the initial implementation: an Agent's quick-reply catalogue is not shared master data the way ticket categories are — it's closer to `AgentTasks`, something an Agent authors and maintains day to day. **Agent should get `quickreplies.manage` too**, giving Agents the same Create/Edit/Delete access as Administrator for this feature. Manager stays `View`-only (unchanged — Manager was never in scope for this ask).

### What changed

- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Roles/Permissions.cs`:
  - `EligibleBySystemRole["AGENT"]` now includes `QuickReplies.Manage` alongside the existing `QuickReplies.View`.
  - `QuickReplies` class XML doc updated to describe `Manage` as Administrator **and** Agent (not Administrator-only).
- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure/Persistence/DbSeeder.cs`:
  - `SeedDefaultRolePermissionsAsync`'s Agent default-grant array now includes `Permissions.QuickReplies.Manage`.
  - New `BackfillQuickRepliesManageForAgentAsync` (mirrors the existing `BackfillPermissionForRolesAsync` helper, `["AGENT"]` only) wired into `SeedAsync()` right after `BackfillQuickRepliesViewAsync`, since installs whose one-time bootstrap already ran won't otherwise pick up the new grant.
- No API, DTO, service, migration, or frontend code changes were needed — the controller already gated Create/Update/Delete on `Permissions.QuickReplies.Manage`; the frontend already reads `hasPermission("quickreplies.manage")` dynamically (`QuickRepliesListPage.tsx`, `QuickReplyFormPage.tsx` route guards in `App.tsx`). Both now light up automatically for Agent once the permission claim is present in the JWT.

### Verification performed

- `dotnet build` / `dotnet test` (123/123, no regressions).
- Live API smoke test as a fresh Agent-role account: `POST`, `PUT`, and `DELETE /api/quick-replies` all succeeded (201/200/204) where they previously returned 403.
- Confirmed Manager's permission set is unaffected (still `View` only).

### Updated acceptance criteria (additive)

- [ ] Agent can access the Quick Replies management screen with full Create/Edit/Delete controls visible (not just the read-only list).
- [ ] Agent can create, edit, and delete quick replies via both the UI and the API (`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/quick-replies`).
- [ ] Manager continues to see the read-only list only — no New/Edit/Delete controls, and the API still returns 403 on write for a Manager-only token.
- [ ] A pre-existing installation (Agent role created before this correction) picks up `quickreplies.manage` automatically on the next application boot via the new backfill — no manual role-permission edit required.
